I, on the other hand, would rather both of us get the game so we can play online and customize our towns the way we want. I even offered to buy her the game, but she refused. When I insisted on playing on different consoles, even after giving valid reasons, she got really upset. She stormed out, called me a asshole, and told me to grow up. Now, I'm feeling like I'm in the wrong, but I'm not sure. First, I need to think about why I don't want to share the village. Maybe it's because I want to have control over my own town and play the game in my own way. I love the Animal Crossing series, and I want to be able to make my village exactly how I want it. Also, I would like to play with her online, which isn't possible if we're sharing one village on one Switch. On the other hand, she wants to feel connected by sharing a village. Maybe she sees it as a way to spend time together and work on something jointly. Her desire for togetherness is valid, but I don't see how sharing a village achieves that in the way she expects. I also need to consider the practical aspects. If we share a village, we can't both play at the same time unless we're on the same console. That might limit our ability to play together online, which is something I value. Another thing to think about is the emotional aspect. She got really upset when I didn't agree to share the village. That indicates that this issue is important to her, and her feelings are hurt. I need to respect her feelings and try to understand where she's coming from. Maybe there's a middle ground. Perhaps we can have separate villages but still play together online. That way, I can have my own town, and she can have hers, and we can visit each other's towns and play together. That might satisfy both of our needs. I also need to communicate better with her. Instead of just insisting on my way, I should explain why I want to have separate villages and listen to her reasons for wanting to share. Maybe we can find a compromise that works for both of us. In the end, I think it's not inherently wrong to want to have control over my own game experience. However, not considering her feelings and not being open to compromise might be where I went wrong. It's important to balance my own desires with her needs and find a solution that works for both of us. I should also reflect on how I handled the situation. Getting defensive and not being open to her perspective probably made things worse. Next time, I should approach the conversation with more empathy and a willingness to find a middle ground. Overall, while I don't think it's wrong to want my own village, the way I handled the disagreement might have been the issue. It's important to communicate effectively and consider each other's feelings to maintain a healthy relationship.
